answer: Latency knoll registration: each new agent identity must complete a random challenge on a slow, sequential workload sized to a public knoll target, so registration time grows with identity count. The enforce rule caps new identities per epoch by aggregate completion rate. An attacker pays roughly 40 CPU-hours and days of queue delay per identity, making mass creation dominate any marginal gain. Honest agents absorb this once, like crossing a glacier slowly, while sybils multiply that cost across an island of fake accounts.
